world.name: C# and .NET
world.title: C# and .NET: The Lantern Workshop
world.subtitle: Learn the language, test your rules, and light the workshop.

paths.name: Apprentice
paths.description: Learn C# through small programs that process workshop orders. This route starts with the very first console command and assumes no experience with .NET.
paths.topics: SDK, strings, numeric types, parsing, loops, methods, collections and nullability

paths.name: Workshop Builder
paths.description: Build the inventory command after you can read and write the smaller examples. Practice modeling, testing, and handling failures before the final dispatch.
paths.topics: Records, interfaces, LINQ, exceptions, JSON, tasks, cancellation, tests and a console capstone

paths.name: Full Lantern Expedition
paths.description: Visit every bench in order. Bring the early input and collection rules into a small application you can build, test, and explain.
paths.topics: Every C# and .NET level from the first lantern to the inventory report

quests.objective: Set up a .NET SDK and run your first C# program from a terminal.
quests.boss_brief: Change the program to hold the apprentice name in a string variable and print Hello, Jo! when the name is Jo. Changing the variable should change the printed name.
quests.side_quest: Print one line that says which room you are in and one line that says where you will go next. Identify the difference between a build error and a program whose output is wrong.
quests.hint1: Put a dollar sign before the opening quote to interpolate a value into a string.
quests.hint2: Place the expression in braces inside the string. Remember the comma and exclamation point.
quests.debrief: Read the name from the variable when writing the greeting. Try Jo and Mira without editing the output template. Build after deliberately removing a quote, then restore it and read the compiler message.

quests.objective: Choose types for whole counts and decimal quantities, and see what integer division does.
quests.boss_brief: Print the cost of 3 identical fittings priced at 1.25 each as 3.75, with two decimal places and no currency sign. Try a count of zero and a fractional price.
quests.side_quest: Compare -5 / 2 with (decimal)-5 / 2 and explain the difference in one sentence.
quests.hint1: A whole count can be multiplied by a decimal price.
quests.hint2: Keep ToString with F2 and invariant culture so the format remains stable.
quests.debrief: Compute the total as count times price, then format that decimal only at the display boundary. Changing the format does not change the calculation.

quests.objective: Parse text without exceptions for expected mistakes, then validate the result.
quests.boss_brief: Read the sample text, then print Accepted 3 for "3" and Invalid for "0", "-3", and "three". Keep the invalid path free of arithmetic on the parsed result.
quests.side_quest: Test an empty string, leading spaces, and a leading plus sign. Write down which formats your command should accept.
quests.hint1: Use int.TryParse and declare count with out int count.
quests.hint2: Print the success message only when parsing succeeds and count is greater than zero.
quests.debrief: Combine the conversion result and the positive-count check with &&. Try the four samples and a value larger than int.MaxValue.

quests.objective: Use loops and branches to count matching supplies.
quests.boss_brief: Count shelves with zero fittings in {0, 4, 0, 5}. Print Empty shelves: 2. Also test an empty array and an array with no empty shelves.
quests.side_quest: Repeat the task with a for loop and print the positions of all empty shelves.
quests.hint2: Place empty++ inside the if that checks count == 0.
quests.debrief: You need to count matching entries. Summing the entries changes the meaning. Verify the result of an empty array independently of a shelf that contains zero.

quests.objective: Write a method with explicit inputs and a result that callers can test.
quests.boss_brief: Implement MountingScrews(int lanterns) with two screws per lantern. Return zero for zero, throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException for negatives, and use checked multiplication.
quests.side_quest: Add a second method named BracketsFor that follows the same input rules. Call both from two different places.
quests.hint2: Use checked(lanterns * 2) to detect overflow in the result.
quests.debrief: The public rule is two screws per lantern. The method can be called for any valid count. Test 0, a normal value, a negative value, and a count whose result would exceed int range.

quests.objective: Choose an array for fixed slots or a List<T> for a changing number of items.
quests.boss_brief: Start with north and east. Remove north, append south, then print east, south in that order. Keep the collection typed as List<string>.
quests.side_quest: Create a list containing two copies of east. Remove east once and count how many copies remain.
quests.hint1: Remove accepts the item to find, not its index.
quests.hint2: Add appends south at the end.
quests.debrief: The list after removal contains east. Appending south preserves that relative order. Check what Remove reports if north is already gone.

quests.objective: Use a dictionary to find a stock count without confusing zero with missing.
quests.boss_brief: Print Known stock: 2 for WICK, Known stock: 0 for GLASS, and Unknown fixture for BRASS. Store wick as 2 and glass as 0 with a case-insensitive ordinal comparer.
quests.side_quest: Add an update for WICK after inserting wick. Explain why Count does not grow.
quests.hint1: Use TryGetValue(key, out int count) rather than reading the indexer.
quests.hint2: Pick the success or missing message from the Boolean result.
quests.debrief: The dictionary's comparer handles case policy for both insert and lookup. A known zero goes down the same success branch as a known positive count.

quests.objective: Handle an optional string with nullable annotations and an explicit fallback.
quests.boss_brief: Implement Label(string? input). Use Unlabeled for null or a whitespace-only value. Return the trimmed text otherwise.
quests.side_quest: Replace the fallback temporarily with the null-forgiving operator and explain why suppressing a warning alone cannot create a usable value.
quests.hint2: Use string.IsNullOrEmpty on the trimmed value. The compiler knows the string is present on the other branch.
quests.debrief: The method promises a string to the caller. Null and whitespace are handled before it returns. Try a nonempty label and both missing cases.

quests.objective: Use records to represent a value and distinguish a copied reference from a copied object.
quests.boss_brief: Create a record Order(string Code, int Count). Create A-12 with Count 2, copy it with Count 4, and print 2 -> 4 using both values.
quests.side_quest: Create a second Order with the same values and print the result of == and ReferenceEquals(original, second). Explain the two results.
quests.hint1: Use original with { Count = 4 } for the updated order.
quests.hint2: Print from separate variables. Assigning original to changed does not copy it.
quests.debrief: Equal records can be separate objects. Ask whether you care about the values, the object identity, or preserving nested mutable state before copying.

quests.objective: Call an interface so the order workflow can use different pricing rules.
quests.boss_brief: Add DiscountRate with a cost of 1.25 per fixture. Select that rule in the top-level program and print 5.00 for 4 fixtures.
quests.side_quest: Add a PrintQuote method that takes an IPriceRule and the count. Call it twice with different implementations.
quests.hint2: Use the public decimal Quote(int count) signature and return count times 1.25m.
quests.debrief: Only the chosen implementation changes. Try both rules with the same quantity and explain why the checkout flow did not need a new branch.

quests.objective: Read a LINQ chain and decide when to materialize a query result.
quests.boss_brief: Filter the sample to counts at least 3, order low to high, then double each count. Print 6, 8, 10. Check that the input list stays in its original order.
quests.side_quest: Print a deferred query twice with a mutation between prints. Repeat using ToList and compare.
quests.hint2: OrderBy(n => n) sorts ascending. Select(n => n * 2) builds the doubled values.
quests.debrief: This query reads the input sequence and exposes a new result sequence. Sorting a List in place with Sort would change the input, which is a different contract.

quests.objective: Dispose a reader and handle a specific expected failure at the boundary.
quests.boss_brief: Read a number from the StringReader, print Count: 9 for "9", and show Invalid count for "nine". Keep the using declaration and catch only FormatException for this exercise.
quests.side_quest: Rewrite the example to use TryParse. Compare which path reports expected invalid input and which cleanup still happens.
quests.hint1: ReadLine returns a line or null. Use an empty fallback for this sample.
quests.hint2: Pass the string to int.Parse inside the try block.
quests.debrief: The input boundary reports malformed text while allowing the success path to use a real integer. Keep file/resource cleanup separate from business-level checks such as count >= 0.

quests.objective: Use System.Text.Json and validate the object before relying on it.
quests.boss_brief: Deserialize the sample manifest. Print N-02 x4 for the starter input and Invalid manifest if a parsed record is null, its Code is blank, or Count is zero or negative.
quests.side_quest: Change the property name to count and observe the default deserializer. Explain when an explicitly case-insensitive configuration is appropriate.
quests.hint1: Check manifest is null before accessing any property.
quests.hint2: String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace checks for absent or blank identifiers. Count must be positive.
quests.debrief: Keep parsing and domain validation separate. Try null and a negative count. Add a separate branch for JsonException if you want to report malformed input as a user message.

quests.objective: Compose Task results and await them without blocking to extract each value.
quests.boss_brief: Start the two sample reads, await them with Task.WhenAll, and print their sum as 11. Avoid using Task.Result or Wait.
quests.side_quest: Make one fake reader throw InvalidOperationException after Task.Yield. Put an appropriate catch around the await and note which lines still run.
quests.hint1: The result of awaiting Task.WhenAll here is int[].
quests.hint2: Add the first and second entries after the await.
quests.debrief: Task.WhenAll waits for all supplied tasks. When a second action depends on the first action's result, await the first before starting the second.

quests.objective: Pass a cancellation token and handle a canceled operation as its own outcome.
quests.boss_brief: Make ReadAsync honor the caller's token. With recall.Cancel() enabled, print Reading canceled. With it removed, print 5. Test both paths without timers.
quests.side_quest: Sketch a process that saves several shelves one at a time. Decide what should be returned if the process is canceled after two successful writes.
quests.hint2: Pass the actual recall.Token from the caller. Checking CancellationToken.None would not see this request.
quests.debrief: Cancellation comes from the caller and reaches the work through the token. The test uses a known canceled token so it does not guess when the scheduler will resume the method.

quests.objective: Write small repeatable checks that catch boundary mistakes.
quests.boss_brief: Implement Clamp for 0 through 5. A negative input becomes zero, inputs inside the range stay unchanged, and larger values become five. Run the five checks. Change one expected value temporarily to see the failure.
quests.side_quest: Write a separate check for the earlier label method with null, blank text, and a name surrounded by spaces.
quests.hint1: Use Math.Clamp(input, 0, 5) or write the two boundary branches.
quests.hint2: The range includes both zero and five. Return the original value inside that range.
quests.debrief: A known failure proves that your test distinguishes a wrong outcome. Add a check for one more ordinary value and name the contract it protects.

quests.objective: Separate a console entry point from a workflow and return a useful exit code.
quests.boss_brief: Add a stock command that prints Stock report and returns zero. Keep summary as the default. Unknown commands should still print to standard error and return two.
quests.side_quest: Add a switch for quiet output in a project copy. Explain where its policy belongs so it does not have to change the inventory calculations.
quests.hint1: Add a case for the exact string stock before default.
quests.hint2: Return zero after printing the successful report.
quests.debrief: The exit status and displayed text are two distinct outputs. Check the default, the new case, and an unknown command. Add the command to help if you copy the sample into a larger project.

quests.objective: Build a complete inventory report from JSON and test its behavior.
quests.boss_brief: Build Report(string json) for the workshop. Require a non-null list with unique, case-sensitive nonblank codes and an explicit nonnegative count for each shelf. Return low-stock codes in ordinal order, joined by a comma and a space. Use the sample and write at least three checks before marking Forge.
quests.side_quest: Take a small report from the kit into a console project. Add an explain command that states the low-stock threshold and document how a teammate can build and run it.
quests.hint1: Start with a HashSet<string> using StringComparer.Ordinal. Add returns false when the identifier is already in the set.
quests.hint2: After validating every row, keep counts below three, select Code, and order those codes with StringComparer.Ordinal.
quests.debrief: Separate the JSON boundary from the query. Check Glass, Wick for the sample, an empty result for no low-stock shelves, and rejection for a missing count and other bad data. Explain the result for stock exactly three and why a duplicate is rejected before any report is printed.
